title_en: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
title_zh: 泽伦斯基称赞乌克兰“史无前例”的袭击，普京的克里米亚大桥部分倒塌
summary: Ukraine says the missile and drone attack on the strategic bridge in the Russian-annexed Crimea took weeks to plan.
summary_zh: 乌克兰表示，针对俄罗斯吞并的克里米亚战略桥梁的导弹和无人机袭击花了数周时间策划。
body_en: By Olivia Ireland , Sarah Rainsford , Southern and Eastern Europe correspondent, Kyiv and Ilya Abishev , BBC News Russian
Ukraine has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, in what President Volodymyr Zelensky says was an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making.
Images shared by Ukrainian officials show a section of the Crimean Bridge collapsed into the water, dealing a logistical and symbolic blow to Moscow's war effort.
The Kremlin said it would rebuild the bridge "better than before".

Meanwhile in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said traffic had partially resumed on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) and Pivdennyi (Southern) bridges - key crossings over the Dnipro River - after they had been closed following Russian strikes overnight.
Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good.

While Kyiv has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Russian President Vladimir Putin.
The timing of the strike comes at a significant moment, ahead of Putin meeting the leaders of China and the US. This could cloud his moment back in the spotlight.
The Crimean Bridge was built by Russia after it invaded and illegally annexed Ukraine's southern peninsula in 2014.

The $3.6bn (£2.7bn) piece of infrastructure is widely seen in Russia and Ukraine as Putin's personal pet project: His close tycoon friend Arkady Rotenberg built it, and then Putin personally opened it by driving a lorry over it in May 2018.
In Ukraine, the much-hated bridge is seen as one of the main symbols of Russia's continuing occupation of Ukrainian lands.
"We're drinking champagne!" Andrii, an engineer who lives in Kyiv, told the BBC.
He said the latest attack would "deal a very heavy blow to the morale of the Russians".

Some Ukrainians are concerned that Putin might now respond by carrying out even more attacks against civilian infrastructure, but Andrii said: "I don't think the Russians can make things much worse; they're already pounding us every single night with everything they've got."

The damage after the overnight attack, involving cruise missiles and drones, appeared to be far more severe than during previous strikes on the bridge, with a large arched section apparently destroyed.
Video footage appeared to show critical damage to the road section, with remnants of the support arch and road deck seen protruding from the water below.

Zelensky said the strike was the result of a seven-stage operation by the military and security services, which saw Ukrainian forces "gradually destroy air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective".
He said several types of Ukrainian drones as well as the country's Flamingo and Neptune cruise missiles were fired overnight during a "pivotal stage".

The Ukrainian president also said the rail section parallel to the bridge's road had also been hit by a wave of drones, though images showed its supporting arch was still standing and Russia's transport ministry later said some rail services resumed.

Ukraine's state security service SBU said its operations had "systematically suppressed enemy air defence systems" over a month, and said it showed "no Russian defence systems can guarantee the safety of illegal objects occupied by the invaders".
body_zh: 作者：Olivia Ireland、Sarah Rainsford、南欧和东欧记者、基辅和 Ilya Abishev、BBC 俄语新闻
乌克兰严重破坏了连接俄罗斯和被占领克里米亚的一座重要桥梁，总统泽伦斯基称这是一次“史无前例的行动”，几周前就已经发生了。
乌克兰官员分享的图像显示，克里米亚大桥的一部分倒塌入水中，对莫斯科的战争努力造成了后勤和象征性的打击。
克里姆林宫表示将“比以前更好”地重建这座桥。
与此同时，基辅市市长维塔利·克里琴科表示，第聂伯河上的重要过境点皮夫尼奇尼（北部）和皮夫登尼（南部）桥梁因俄罗斯连夜袭击而关闭，交通已部分恢复。
乌克兰长期以来一直瞄准克里米亚大桥，该大桥为前往前线的俄罗斯士兵提供了公路和铁路路线，但一直在努力永久关闭它。
虽然基辅一直试图通过打击炼油厂和仓库来增加俄罗斯发动战争的经济成本，但袭击桥梁则是试图增加俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京的政治成本。
这次袭击的时机恰逢普京会见中国和美国领导人之前的一个重要时刻。这可能会让他重新回到聚光灯下。
克里米亚大桥是俄罗斯在2014年入侵并非法吞并乌克兰南部半岛后修建的。
这座价值 36 亿美元（27 亿英镑）的基础设施在俄罗斯和乌克兰被广泛视为普京的私人项目：他的密友阿尔卡迪·罗滕贝格建造了它，然后普京于 2018 年 5 月驾驶一辆卡车在上面亲自开通。
在乌克兰，这座令人痛恨的桥梁被视为俄罗斯持续占领乌克兰土地的主要象征之一。
“我们正在喝香槟！”居住在基辅的工程师安德里 (Andrii) 告诉英国广播公司 (BBC)。
他表示，最近的袭击将“对俄罗斯人的士气造成非常沉重的打击”。
一些乌克兰人担心普京现在可能会对民用基础设施发动更多袭击作为回应，但安德里说：“我认为俄罗斯人不会让事情变得更糟；他们已经每晚都在用他们所拥有的一切攻击我们。”
这次夜间袭击涉及巡航导弹和无人机，造成的破坏似乎比之前袭击桥梁时严重得多，一大片拱形部分明显被毁。
视频片段似乎显示路段受到严重损坏，支撑拱和路面的残余物从下面的水中突出。
泽连斯基表示，这次袭击是军队和安全部门分七阶段行动的结果，乌克兰军队“在到达最终目标的过程中逐步摧毁防空系统、雷达、电子战设备和其他指定目标”。
他说，在“关键阶段”，乌克兰的几种类型的无人机以及该国的火烈鸟和海王星巡航导弹在夜间发射。
乌克兰总统还表示，与大桥道路平行的铁路段也遭到无人机浪潮的袭击，不过图像显示其支撑拱门仍然矗立，俄罗斯交通部后来表示，部分铁路服务已恢复。
乌克兰国家安全局SBU表示，其行动在一个多月内“系统地压制了敌方防空系统”，并表示“俄罗斯的任何防御系统都无法保证入侵者占领的非法物体的安全”。

title_en: Ukraine strikes major Russian bridge with drones and missiles as aerial attacks escalate
title_zh: 随着空袭升级，乌克兰用无人机和导弹袭击了俄罗斯主要桥梁
summary: Ukrainian drones and missiles struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimean, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, as Russia reported its forces downed Ukrainian drones.
summary_zh: 乌克兰总统泽连斯基表示，乌克兰无人机和导弹袭击了连接俄罗斯和被占领克里米亚的刻赤大桥
body_en: A freight train runs on rails of a railway link of the Crimean Bridge connecting Russian mainland and the Crimean Peninsula over the Kerch Strait not far from Kerch, Crimea, on July 17, 2023. AP hide caption

KYIV, Ukraine — Ukrainian drones and missiles struck the vital Kerch Bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Tuesday, calling it an "unprecedented" operation as Russia reported that its forces downed a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day.
Trump's envoys hope to get Europe involved in Russia-Ukraine peace talks

Zelenskyy portrayed the bridge operation as a masterstroke following a weekslong effort by Ukrainian forces to gradually wear down Russian air defenses before bombarding the prized target with a barrage of missiles and drones overnight.

Zelenskyy didn't detail the damage, but the Ukrainian General Staff said that an arch and a span of the bridge's road section collapsed, severing the road link, while the railway line was still standing but with a damaged arch.
Russia's Investigative Committee, the nation's top criminal investigation agency, said the bridge was attacked by drones and sustained damage but didn't elaborate.
How AI drones are influencing the course of the Ukraine war

The Kerch Bridge is a crucial link in moving military and civilian supplies from Russia to Crimea and for supporting troops on the front line. The construction of the bridge, a potent symbol of Russia's illegal annexation of the peninsula in 2014, was inflammatory to Ukrainians.
"The symbol of the occupation has cracked," the Ukrainian General Staff said in a statement.
Moscow's forces, meanwhile, fired ballistic missiles and drones at Kyiv, hitting two of the Ukrainian capital's main bridges and killing at least two people.

A recent escalation in aerial attacks came as Russia and Ukraine await a date for the next round of U.S.-mediated talks aimed at ending the war that began with Moscow's full-scale invasion of its neighbor on Feb. 24, 2022.

U.S. President Donald Trump says he plans to talk about the war in Ukraine during his highly anticipated meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in China this week.
Missiles delivered the final blow in the 7-stage operation
The Kerch Bridge attack was the culmination of weeks of preparatory strikes over seven stages of the operation, Zelenskyy said on social media.
Kushner and Witkoff renew peace talks to end war between Russia and Ukraine
Ukrainian forces knocked out defense systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment and other designated targets before launching Monday night's final attack, he said.

Domestically developed long-range drones struck the bridge's road section during the night while Ukraine's Neptune missiles and other drones aimed at the rail section, he said. Precision-guided Flamingo missiles delivered the final blow, he said.

Zelenskyy and the Ukrainian military published videos showing what they said were the attacks and subsequent damage to the bridge, with part of the deck in the water and a fallen arch. The Associated Press wasn't able to verify the images.
The Russian-installed governor of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, said traffic across the bridge was halted but rail traffic was restored by Tuesday afternoon. He didn't mention any damage.
body_zh: 2023 年 7 月 17 日，一列货运列车在距离克里米亚刻赤不远的刻赤海峡上连接俄罗斯大陆和克里米亚半岛的克里米亚大桥铁路线上运行。美联社隐藏标题栏
乌克兰基辅——乌克兰总统泽连斯基周二表示，乌克兰无人机和导弹袭击了连接俄罗斯和被占领克里米亚半岛的重要刻赤大桥，并称这是一次“史无前例”的行动，因为俄罗斯报告称，乌克兰军队连续第二天击落的乌克兰无人机数量创历史新高。
特朗普的特使希望让欧洲参与俄罗斯与乌克兰的和谈
泽连斯基将这次桥梁行动描述为乌克兰军队在长达一周的努力中逐步削弱俄罗斯防空系统，然后在夜间用一系列导弹和无人机轰炸这一重要目标之后的一次绝妙的行动。
泽连斯基没有详细说明损坏情况，但乌克兰总参谋部表示，桥梁路段的一个拱门和一个跨度倒塌，切断了道路连接，而铁路线仍然存在，但拱门受损。
俄罗斯最高刑事调查机构俄罗斯调查委员会表示，这座桥遭到无人机袭击并遭受损坏，但没有详细说明。
人工智能无人机如何影响乌克兰战争的进程
刻赤大桥是从俄罗斯向克里米亚运送军事和民用物资以及支援前线部队的重要纽带。这座大桥的建设是俄罗斯 2014 年非法吞并半岛的有力象征，对乌克兰人来说具有煽动性。
乌克兰总参谋部在一份声明中表示：“占领的象征已经破裂。”
与此同时，莫斯科军队向基辅发射弹道导弹和无人机，击中乌克兰首都的两座主要桥梁，造成至少两人死亡。
最近空袭升级之际，俄罗斯和乌克兰正在等待美国斡旋的下一轮会谈的日期，该会谈旨在结束因莫斯科于 2022 年 2 月 24 日全面入侵其邻国而开始的战争。
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，他计划本周在中国与中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统普京举行备受期待的会晤，期间讨论乌克兰战争。
导弹在七阶段行动中给予最后一击
泽连斯基在社交媒体上表示，刻赤大桥袭击事件是长达数周、七个阶段的准备性打击的高潮。
库什纳和维特科夫重启和平谈判以结束俄罗斯和乌克兰之间的战争
他说，乌克兰军队在周一晚上发动最后一次攻击之前摧毁了防御系统、雷达、电子战设备和其他指定目标。
他说，国内开发的远程无人机在夜间袭击了大桥的路段，而乌克兰的海王星导弹和其他无人机则瞄准了铁路段。他说，精确制导火烈鸟导弹给予了最后一击。
泽伦斯基和乌克兰军方发布了视频，显示了他们所说的袭击事件以及随后对桥梁的损坏，部分桥面浸入水中，拱门倒塌。美联社无法核实这些图像。
俄罗斯任命的克里米亚总督谢尔盖·阿克肖诺夫表示，大桥上的交通已停止，但铁路交通已于周二下午恢复。他没有提到任何损坏。

title_en: 'It was really scary': Mother describes sheltering during Russia strikes on Kyiv bridge
title_zh: “这真的很可怕”：母亲描述俄罗斯袭击基辅大桥期间的庇护
summary: Moscow has targeted bridges in Kyiv, while Ukraine severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea.
summary_zh: 莫斯科以基辅的桥梁为目标，而乌克兰则严重损坏了连接俄罗斯和被占领克里米亚的一座重要桥梁。
body_en: By Sarah Rainsford , Southern and Eastern Europe correspondent , Mariana Matveichuk and Marianne Baisnee , Reporting from Kyiv
The alarms warning of a ballistic missile threat went off just before 23:30 on Monday in Kyiv. Moments later came the boom of explosions.
Once again, the main bridges over the broad River Dnipro that cuts through the city were the target and this time the Russian missiles hit what they wanted.
Close to one end of the Pivnichnyi (Northern) bridge there is a large crater and in the pouring rain, water now rushes through it to the river below. Chunks of tarmac and metal are scattered around.
At its broadest point, the jagged hole is about eight metres wide.

The crossing is closed to all traffic apart from the occasional fire engine or police car passing at high speed. By contrast, nearby roads are jammed with cars and trucks, forced to take long detours.
Anyone in a hurry to move around this city has to walk, or cycle, across the bridge, picking their way through the wreckage. In the miserable weather, that also means getting very wet.
Masha and her family moved to a flat next to the bridge because they had been living by a power plant that kept getting hit by Russian missiles.
Last night, she was in the kitchen of their new place when the Russians struck the bridge. She thought her windows would be blown out of their frames by the explosions.
"It was really scary. We had no idea they'd hit here so much. It's like we're cursed," Masha told me, describing grabbing her child and running into the corridor for protection.
But somehow, she still managed to sound cheerful.
"It's difficult, but we're used to it. And we try to take the positive from everything. Like: we survived today! So we can be happy about that."
From the damage, it looks like Russia targeted the same spot on the bridge with a volley of three missiles, aiming to keep the road closed for as long as possible.

A major recovery operation is under way, with firefighters and engineers in fluorescent overalls working to evaluate the extent of the damage. But it looks like the disruption will continue for some time.
Further along the Dnipro River, the Pivdennyi (Southern) bridge was also hit on Monday night, with four missiles.

The metro line across it was suspended for a while, although by mid-afternoon it had been restored. The mayor, Vitali Klitschko, said road transport in one direction was also being partially restored.
On the Pivnichnyi bridge, a man with a bag of tennis rackets on his back was gazing at the crater in front of him. He was heading home from the courts after he had travelled on foot to the left bank.
"It is upsetting," Anatolii told us. "Then when you read the news of what our side did to the Crimea bridge, you do feel a bit better."
That is because there was a battle of the bridges overnight.

Ukrainian missiles hit the one Russia had built to occupied Crimea, and caused serious damage. That bridge is prized by Russian President Vladimir Putin personally, a symbol of his illegal 2014 takeover.
body_zh: 作者：Sarah Rainsford，南欧和东欧记者，Mariana Matveichuk 和 Marianne Baisnee，基辅报道
周一 23:30 之前，基辅弹道导弹威胁警报响起。片刻之后，爆炸声传来。
穿过城市的宽阔第聂伯罗河上的主要桥梁再次成为目标，这一次俄罗斯导弹击中了他们想要的目标。
靠近 Pivnichnyi（北）桥的一端有一个大火山口，在倾盆大雨中，水现在通过它流入下面的河流。大块的柏油路和金属散落在周围。
这个锯齿状的洞最宽处大约有八米宽。
除了偶尔高速驶过的消防车或警车外，该十字路口禁止所有车辆通行。相比之下，附近的道路上挤满了汽车和卡车，被迫绕很远的路。
任何急于在这座城市中走动的人都必须步行或骑自行车过桥，在废墟中寻找出路。在恶劣的天气下，这也意味着会变得很湿。
玛莎和她的家人搬到了桥旁边的一套公寓，因为他们住在一座发电厂附近，经常受到俄罗斯导弹的袭击。
昨晚，当俄罗斯人袭击大桥时，她正在新住所的厨房里。她认为爆炸会把她的窗户从窗框上炸掉。
“这真的很可怕。我们不知道他们会袭击这里这么多。就像我们被诅咒了一样，”玛莎告诉我，她抓住了她的孩子，跑进走廊寻求保护。
但不知何故，她听起来仍然很高兴。
“这很困难，但我们已经习惯了。我们尝试从一切事情中获得积极的一面。比如：我们今天活了下来！所以我们可以为此感到高兴。”
从损坏情况来看，俄罗斯似乎向桥上的同一地点发射了三枚导弹，旨在尽可能长时间地保持道路封闭。
一项重大的恢复行动正在进行中，身穿荧光工作服的消防员和工程师正在评估损坏程度。但看来这种混乱还将持续一段时间。
周一晚上，沿着第聂伯罗河，皮夫登尼（南部）大桥也遭到四枚导弹袭击。
穿过它的地铁线路暂停了一段时间，不过到下午三点左右就恢复了。市长维塔利·克里琴科 (Vitali Klitschko) 表示，单向道路交通也已部分恢复。
皮夫尼奇桥上，一名男子背着一袋网球拍，凝视着面前的火山口。步行到左岸后，他正在从法院回家的路上。
“这令人不安，”阿纳托利告诉我们。 “然后，当你读到我们方面对克里米亚大桥所做的事情的新闻时，你确实会感觉好一点。”
那是因为一夜之间发生了一场桥梁之战。
乌克兰导弹击中了俄罗斯为被占领的克里米亚建造的导弹，造成了严重破坏。这座桥受到俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京 (Vladimir Putin) 个人的珍视，成为他 2014 年非法接管的象征。

title_en: How the attack on Crimean Bridge unfolded
title_zh: 克里米亚大桥袭击事件是如何展开的
summary: One of the key symbols of Russia's occupation of Ukraine has suffered major damage after a seven-stage attack by Kyiv.
summary_zh: 俄罗斯占领乌克兰的关键标志之一在基辅发动七阶段袭击后遭受重大破坏。
body_en: By Laura Gozzi , Ilya Abishev , BBC Russian Defence Correspondent and Richard Irvine-Brown , BBC Verify

Stretching across the Kerch Strait in the Black Sea, the Crimean Bridge was always a symbol: for Russia, a prestige project cementing its claim to sovereign Ukrainian territory, and for Ukraine, a hated piece of infrastructure emblematic of Moscow's occupation of the Crimean Peninsula.

A key section of the double-arched, 12-mile-long bridge now lies on the seabed, brought down by an arsenal of Ukrainian long-range weaponry in a seven-stage operation culminating in a dramatic collapse.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has said that the bridge "will be rebuilt, and it will be even better than before".
But eight years after its unveiling, the bridge has now become material proof of Kyiv's ability to pierce through Moscow's military defences to hit even its most treasured and protected structures.
The attack on the strategic Crimean Bridge was carried out gradually to cut across several layers of defence, Kyiv confirmed on Tuesday.

For several weeks Ukraine's Security Service and its General Staff gradually destroyed air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare assets, and other designated targets, President Volodymyr Zelensky said.

A significant strike had already been reported on 16 November , when drones hit the bridge at night. Traffic was paused briefly then reinstated, and although the arch over the road section was visibly damaged, the structure remained standing.
But that hit turned out to have been only the penultimate stage of a complex attack.
In the early hours of 17 November, the final strikes dealt a fatal blow to the weakened arch structure.

One verified video - filmed from a camera on board a Ukrainian-made Flamingo missile - shows the weapon approaching the main span of the bridge and heading towards the steel arches, with the footage freezing just before impact.

The Flamingo had potentially been modified to be controlled remotely, which improved its accuracy enough to strike the bridge supports, munitions expert Justin Bronk, from the Royal United Services Institute said.
The missile's "very heavy warhead" made it "more suitable" for attacking the bridge's reinforced concrete spans and supports, Bronk added.

Zelensky later confirmed that several types of missiles and drones had been employed in the attack, which led the massive road arch - weighing thousands of tonnes and measuring about 227m in length - to collapse into the strait.
Daylight images taken from the shores of Crimea to the north show a section about 200m (660ft) long of the tarmac was too dragged below into the sea.

This is clearly critical damage to the crossing. Far from just being a decorative feature of the bridge, the arch played a structural role, transferring loads and supporting the span and helping to ensure the stability of the entire structure.

The parallel arch supporting the railway section has remained standing, although it may also have been damaged. All traffic on the bridge was initially suspended, though trains were later allowed to resume running.

But the damage to the bridge's main span is "catastrophic", Colin Capriani, a structural engineer from Monash University in Melbourne, Australia, told BBC Verify. It was "very hard to envisage" how the bridge could be rebuilt given it is clearly well within range of Ukrainian weaponry, Capriani added.
Major attacks in 2022 and 2023 had already caused serious damage to the road spans of the bridge, but the structure survived.

The difference this time is "the most critical and vulnerable part of the bridge has been hit", said David MacKenzie of engineering consultancy COWI, adding that "although the wreckage of the bridge can be cleared fairly quickly, reinstating full road traffic will take over a year".
body_zh: 作者：Laura Gozzi、Ilya Abishev，BBC 俄罗斯国防记者；Richard Irvine-Brown，BBC verify
克里米亚大桥横跨黑海刻赤海峡，一直是一个象征：对俄罗斯来说，这是一个巩固其对乌克兰主权领土主张的声望工程，而对乌克兰来说，则是一个令人讨厌的基础设施，象征着莫斯科占领克里米亚半岛。
这座 12 英里长的双拱桥的一个关键部分现在位于海底，在七阶段行动中被乌克兰远程武器库击落，最终导致戏剧性的倒塌。
克里姆林宫发言人德米特里·佩斯科夫表示，这座桥“将被重建，而且会比以前更好”。
但在揭幕八年后，这座桥现已成为基辅有能力突破莫斯科军事防御，甚至袭击其最珍贵和最受保护的建筑的物质证明。
基辅周二证实，对具有战略意义的克里米亚大桥的袭击是逐步进行的，以突破多层防御。
总统泽连斯基表示，几周来，乌克兰安全部门及其总参谋部逐渐摧毁了防空系统、雷达、电子战资产和其他指定目标。
据报道，11 月 16 日，无人机在夜间袭击了大桥，造成了严重的袭击。交通短暂暂停然后恢复，尽管路段上的拱门明显受损，但结构仍然矗立。
但事实证明，那次袭击只是复杂攻击的倒数第二阶段。
11月17日凌晨，最后的攻击对脆弱的拱门结构造成了致命的打击。
一段经过验证的视频是由乌克兰制造的火烈鸟导弹上的摄像机拍摄的，显示武器接近桥梁的主跨并向钢拱门前进，镜头在撞击前冻结。
英国皇家联合军种研究所的弹药专家贾斯汀·布朗克表示，“火烈鸟”可能经过改造，可以进行远程控制，从而提高其精确度，足以击中桥梁支架。
布朗克补充说，导弹的“非常重的弹头”使其“更适合”攻击桥梁的钢筋混凝土跨度和支架。
泽伦斯基后来证实，袭击中使用了多种类型的导弹和无人机，导致重达数千吨、长约 227m 的巨大公路拱门塌入海峡。
从克里米亚北部海岸拍摄的日光图像显示，一段约 200m（660 英尺）长的停机坪被拖入海中。
这显然是对道口的严重破坏。拱不仅仅是桥梁的装饰特征，它还发挥着结构作用，传递荷载和支撑跨度，并有助于确保整个结构的稳定性。
支撑铁路段的平行拱门仍然矗立着，尽管它也可能已被损坏。大桥上的所有交通最初都被暂停，但火车后来被允许恢复运行。
但澳大利亚墨尔本莫纳什大学的结构工程师科林·卡普里亚尼 (Colin Capriani) 告诉 BBC verify，桥梁主跨的损坏是“灾难性的”。卡普里亚尼补充说，“很难想象”如何重建这座桥，因为它显然完全在乌克兰武器的射程之内。
2022 年和 2023 年的重大袭击已经对桥梁的路跨造成了严重损坏，但结构幸存了下来。
工程咨询公司 COWI 的戴维·麦肯齐 (David MacKenzie) 表示，这次的不同之处在于“桥梁最关键、最脆弱的部分受到了影响”，并补充道，“虽然桥梁残骸可以相当快地清除，但恢复全面道路交通需要一年多的时间”。

title_en: UK hands NATO-assigned US soldier accused of Russia spying to US military

body_en: UK hands NATO-assigned US soldier accused of Russia spying to US military | Espionage News | Al Jazeera
Share UK hands NATO-assigned US soldier accused of Russia spying to US military on social media
A senior United States soldier assigned to NATO who was arrested in Britain last week on suspicion of spying for Russia has been transferred to US military custody, United Kingdom police have said.

The Head of Counter Terrorism Police (CTP), Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, said on Tuesday that authorities in London have passed the investigation to US partners “in line with existing international protocols”.

The 41-year-old man was arrested by British police on November 10 near Gloucester on suspicion of offences under Section 1 and Section 3 of the UK National Security Act 2023.
Section 1 relates to obtaining or disclosing protected information, while Section 3 relates to assisting a foreign intelligence service.

“These are extremely serious allegations, and our collective response should send a strong message that we will act swiftly and robustly where we suspect this kind of espionage activity taking place,” Taylor said.
He added, “We will continue to support our US colleagues as they take the matter forwards.”

US FBI Director Kash Patel said the army officer is in US custody as a “result of an espionage investigation” between the FBI’s Philadelphia field office and Legat London in addition to partners at “UK Counter Terrorism Policing, MI5, UK Defence Counter Intelligence, and the US Army Counterintelligence Command.”

Brigadier General Sean Stinchon, the commanding general of US Army Counterintelligence Command (ACIC), said the case illustrated the “remarkable partnership” between ACIC, US Army prosecutors, the FBI, the US Department of Justice, and the UK.
Stinchon added that this example sends a “stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath”.
The case is believed to be the first time a US soldier was found to be under suspicion of spying for a foreign government while in the UK.

第 1 节涉及获取或披露受保护信息，第 3 节涉及协助外国情报部门。

美国陆军反情报司令部司令肖恩·斯廷琼准将也表示，此案展示了“反情报界的决心”。

据信，此案是美国士兵首次在英国被发现涉嫌为外国政府从事间谍活动。

title_en: Russian military plane crashes, killing all 19 on board
title_zh: 俄罗斯军机坠毁 机上19人全部遇难
summary: Russia's defence ministry says it preliminarily believes a technical malfunction was the cause of the crash in the Kemerovo region.
summary_zh: 俄罗斯国防部表示，初步认为克麦罗沃地区坠机事故是技术故障造成的。
body_en: Russian military plane crashes in Siberia killing all 19 on board - BBC News
A Russian military transport plane has crashed in Siberia, killing all 19 people on board, the country's defence ministry said, according to state-run media.
The An-12 aircraft went down during a "scheduled flight" in an "uninhabited area" in the Kemerovo region, the ministry said in a statement.
The ministry added that it preliminarily believed a technical malfunction was the cause of Tuesday's crash. An investigation by Russia's aviation authorities is now under way.
Local Governor Ilya Seredyuk said an emergency response team "quickly extinguished a blaze" after the crash near the village of Yagunovo, and the area was sealed off by police.
Seredyuk, who visited the crash site, said "a helicopter and medical facilities have been put on standby".
The governor added that the "main task" now was to help investigators carry out their work.
He also posted a video showing firefighters combing through what looked like the crash debris, with a number of ambulances also seen standing nearby.

CCTV footage posted on social media appeared to show the moment the plane crashed, with a lighted object falling through the sky in the distance. An explosion then lit up the sky, but the crash was too far away to be seen.
The BBC and Reuters news agency verified the time and date of the footage, while Reuters also verified the location based on features of the scenery that matched satellite imagery of the area.
It was not immediately known whether the crashed aircraft had any cargo on board.
An-12 planes are widely used by the Russian military to transport weaponry and personnel, and also for search and rescue operations.
body_zh: 俄罗斯军用飞机在西伯利亚坠毁，机上19人全部遇难 -_澳门赌博平台

该部补充说，初步认为技术故障是周二坠机的原因。俄罗斯航空当局目前正在进行调查。

英国广播公司（BBC）和路透社证实了这段视频的时间和日期，而路透社也根据与该地区卫星图像相匹配的风景特征验证了该地点。

title_en: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
title_zh: 卫生部称，72 岁巴勒斯坦妇女在约旦河西岸被以色列定居者枪杀
summary: Palestinians say there was an attack by settlers in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, while the Israeli military says the settlers fired after being attacked.
summary_zh: 巴勒斯坦人称，杜尤克塔赫塔的定居者发动了袭击，而以色列军方则表示，定居者在受到袭击后开枪。
body_en: By Yolande Knell , Middle East correspondent , Reporting from Jerusalem and David Gritten

A Palestinian woman in her 70s has been shot dead, and several other people wounded, in a village in the occupied West Bank where Israeli settlers recently moved in, the Palestinian health ministry says.

There are conflicting accounts of what happened. Local Palestinians said there was an attack by settlers in part of al-Duyuk al-Tahta, near Jericho, which is meant to be under the full control of the Palestinian Authority.

According to the Israeli army, there was a Palestinian car-ramming attack on an Israeli vehicle. It said rocks were then thrown at the Israelis, who opened fire in response. It did not mention the fatal shooting of a woman.
There have been high tensions in the area since a group of settlers recently set up a new outpost.
They moved into eight houses in the village on 4 November after buying them, they have said, in a secretive operation. The properties are in an area where Israel retains full security control.
All settlements are illegal under international law.
UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements

Local Palestinians said that the events in al-Duyuk al-Tahta on Monday night began with harassment by Israeli settlers. Palestinian children threw stones, they said, and the settlers opened fire, killing Fadda al-Fahidat, who was 72, outside her home.
Fadda's daughter-in-law, Nema al-Fahidat, told the BBC that she died from a single bullet wound to the head. "It destroyed her brain," she said.

According to the Palestinian accounts, Fadda's son, Arafat, rushed to the scene in his car after hearing the news and collided with an empty Israeli settler car parked outside his family home, injuring settlers who were standing nearby. The settlers then fired more shots, they said, injuring several Palestinians, including Arafat.
"My husband, when he saw his mother, was not paying attention. He crashed into the vehicle. The vehicle was empty," Nema said.
"My husband got out of his car and tried to reach his mother and the injured young men. Then he was shot."

She added: "We tried to gather the injured people and move them away from the settler. We brought them here. But he kept firing, firing, firing. Even after we had brought the wounded young men here and moved them away from him, he continued shooting."
Nema said young Palestinians threw stones at the settlers after seeing what happened, but asked: "What can stones do against bullets?"

The statement from the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said that "terrorists accelerated their vehicle toward an Israeli vehicle and rammed it", and then "exited their vehicle with weapons and attacked and harmed the occupants of the Israeli vehicle".
Afterwards, it said, "rocks were hurled at the Israelis, who responded by firing in order to remove the threat."
Later, an Israeli military source said Fadda was shot by an Israeli civilian and that there was no evidence that she had been involved in the confrontation near her home.
Meanwhile, a spokesperson for Israel's police force said it had opened an investigation, and that officers and forensic technicians had been collecting evidence and interviewing witnesses.

The Israeli human rights group B'Tselem says there has been a prolonged campaign of settler attacks, intimidation and land seizures in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, with Israeli troops now stationed nearby to secure the new settlement.
body_zh: 中东记者 Yolande Knell 和 David Gritten 报道
巴勒斯坦卫生部称，在以色列定居者最近搬入的被占领约旦河西岸的一个村庄里，一名 70 多岁的巴勒斯坦妇女被枪杀，另有几人受伤。
对于所发生的事情，存在着相互矛盾的说法。当地巴勒斯坦人表示，杰里科附近的杜尤克塔赫塔地区发生了定居者的袭击，该地区本应由巴勒斯坦权力机构完全控制。
据以色列军方称，巴勒斯坦人用汽车撞撞了一辆以色列车辆。据称，随后有人向以色列人投掷石块，以色列人开枪回应。它没有提到一名妇女被枪杀的事件。
自从一群定居者最近建立了一个新的前哨基地以来，该地区的局势一直十分紧张。
他们说，他们在一次秘密行动中购买了村里的八栋房子，并于 11 月 4 日搬入其中。这些财产位于以色列保留全面安全控制的地区。
根据国际法，所有定居点都是非法的。
英国制裁以色列约旦河西岸定居点公司
当地巴勒斯坦人表示，周一晚上杜尤克塔赫塔发生的事件始于以色列定居者的骚扰。他们说，巴勒斯坦儿童投掷石块，定居者开枪射杀了 72 岁的法达·法希达 (Fadda al-Fahidat) 。
法达的儿媳 Nema al-Fahidat 告诉 BBC，她死于头部中弹。 “这摧毁了她的大脑，”她说。
据巴勒斯坦方面的报道，法达的儿子阿拉法特闻讯后驾车赶到现场，与停在他家外的一辆空的以色列定居者汽车相撞，导致站在附近的定居者受伤。他们说，定居者随后又开了更多枪，打伤了包括阿拉法特在内的几名巴勒斯坦人。
“我丈夫看到他母亲时，没有注意。他撞上了车。车里是空的，”内马说。
“我的丈夫下了车，试图联系他的母亲和受伤的年轻人。然后他被枪杀了。”
她补充说：“我们试图聚集受伤的人，把他们从定居者身边移开。我们把他们带到了这里。但他一直开枪、开枪、开枪。即使我们把受伤的年轻人带到这里并将他们从他身边移开，他仍然继续开枪。”
内马说，年轻的巴勒斯坦人在看到发生的事情后向定居者投掷石块，但问道：“石头能抵挡子弹吗？”
以色列国防军（IDF）的声明称，“恐怖分子加速车辆冲向一辆以色列车辆并撞击它”，然后“携带武器下车，袭击并伤害了以色列车辆的乘客”。
声明称，事后，“有人向以色列人投掷石块，以色列人则开枪回应，以消除威胁。”
随后，以色列军方消息人士称，法达被一名以色列平民枪杀，没有证据表明她参与了家附近的对峙。
与此同时，以色列警察部队发言人表示，他们已展开调查，警官和法医技术人员一直在收集证据并采访证人。
以色列人权组织 B'Tselem 表示，al-Duyuk al-Tahta 的定居者发动了长期的袭击、恐吓和没收土地活动，以色列军队现在驻扎在附近，以确保新定居点的安全。

title_en: Trump in Asia ahead of talks with Russian and Chinese presidents
title_zh: 特朗普在与俄罗斯和中国总统会谈之前访问亚洲
summary: The US president said he would be open to a one-on-one meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin "if it's available".
summary_zh: 美国总统表示，“如果有可能”，他愿意与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京进行一对一的会面。
body_en: Trump in Manila ahead of talks with Putin and Xi in China - BBC News
South East Asia correspondent , Reporting from Manila

US President Donald Trump has arrived in the Philippines' capital on the first leg of a trip to Asia, which will end in a meeting in China with its President Xi Jinping and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin.
A red carpet was rolled out for Trump as he walked off Air Force One in Manila. A band played one of his favourite songs, Y.M.C.A., before he was whisked away by helicopter to a hotel.

Trump's first meeting at the Asean Summit was with US partners in the Quad - India's Narendra Modi, whom he described as a "very tough man", Japan's Sanae Takaichi, who "may be even tougher", and Australia's Anthony Albanese.
"Our countries are the four corners of the free, open, stable, prosperous Indo-Pacific," the US president said.
"We have outstanding relationships and co-ordinate closely... my phone is always open," Trump added.

Many countries in South East Asia have been hit hard by Trump's tariffs and his war on Iran - but their exports to the US rose 30% last year thanks to the AI boom for which the region manufactures many of the components.
The US is hoping to draw more countries here into its "Pax Silica" tech and AI ecosystem, and away from China.
But China's huge influence in this region cannot easily be challenged, and certainly not in the few hours Trump is in the Philippines.
Later on Tuesday, Trump signed a trade deal with Thailand alongside the country's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul.
The US is Thailand's largest export market, accounting for 24% of its total shipments this year.
Trump then joined South East Asia leaders at a dinner, telling those gathered: "This is one of the world's most vibrant and productive regions filled with the tremendous potential."
After an overnight stay in Manila, the US president will fly to Shenzhen in China to attend a summit of Asia Pacific leaders and have nuclear talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.
Asked if he would also be open to a one-on-one meeting with Putin, Trump said: "If it's available, I would".

东南亚记者，马尼拉报道
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普抵达菲律宾首都，这是亚洲之行的第一站，他的亚洲之行最后将在中国与中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统普京举行会晤。
当特朗普在马尼拉走下空军一号时，人们为他铺上了红地毯。在他被直升机送往一家酒店之前，一支乐队演奏了他最喜欢的一首歌曲《基督教青年会》(Y.M.C.A.)。
特朗普在东盟峰会上的首次会面是与四国集团中的美国伙伴——他形容莫迪为“非常强硬的人”的印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪、“可能更强硬”的日本高市早苗和澳大利亚的安东尼·阿尔巴内塞。
美国总统说：“我们两国是自由、开放、稳定、繁荣的印太地区的四个角落。”
特朗普补充道：“我们关系良好，协调密切……我的电话始终畅通。”
东南亚的许多国家都受到特朗普关税和对伊朗战争的沉重打击，但由于人工智能的蓬勃发展，这些国家对美国的出口去年增长了 30%，而该地区的许多零部件都由该地区生产。
美国希望吸引更多国家加入其“Pax Silica”技术和人工智能生态系统，远离中国。
但中国在该地区的巨大影响力不可能轻易受到挑战，尤其是在特朗普访问菲律宾的几个小时内。
周二晚些时候，特朗普与泰国总理阿努廷·查维拉库尔 (Anutin Charnvirakul) 一起与泰国签署了贸易协议。
美国是泰国最大的出口市场，占今年泰国总出货量的24%。
随后，特朗普与东南亚领导人一起参加晚宴，他告诉与会者：“这是世界上最具活力和生产力的地区之一，充满了巨大潜力。”
在马尼拉过夜后，美国总统将飞往中国深圳出席亚太领导人峰会，并与习近平和普京进行核会谈。
当被问及他是否愿意与普京进行一对一会面时，特朗普表示：“如果有空，我会的。”

title_en: Back to 1997: Russia wants NATO to roll back its eastern expansion
title_zh: 回到1997年：俄罗斯希望北约停止东扩
summary: The Kremlin is reportedly calling on NATO to withdraw from large parts of Eastern Europe. What this would mean for the security of millions of Europeans — and what lies behind Russia's plan.
summary_zh: 据报道，克里姆林宫呼吁北约从东欧大部分地区撤军。这对数百万欧洲人的安全意味着什么
body_en: During talks on ending the war in Ukraine , Russian representatives in Abu Dhabi presented a document containing far-reaching demands, The New York Times reports.

Dated November 10, the document reportedly calls not only for an end to Western arms deliveries to Ukraine but also for NATO to withdraw its troops and bases and move them back to where they were in 1997.

The year 1997 refers to the NATO alliance before its first eastward expansion, according to the Kremlin. At the time, NATO had 16 members. Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary had already been invited to join but did not formally become members of the defense alliance until two years later. In the following years, more countries in Central, Eastern and Southeastern Europe joined, followed most recently by countries in Scandinavia. Today, NATO has 32 member states in Europe and North America.
According to the report, Russia is not explicitly demanding that Central and Eastern European countries leave , but rather that the NATO alliance end its military presence in those countries.
What would be the consequences of a NATO withdrawal?

A withdrawal of NATO troops and bases from member states that joined the alliance after 1997 would significantly weaken their defense capabilities. For example, since 2004, NATO allies, including Germany, have taken turns policing the airspace over Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.

Because the Baltic states do not have fighter jets of their own for independent air policing, NATO provides the capability. Since 2026, the mission has been part of a broader air defense presence. The planned deployment of the German Lithuania Brigade, which is expected to be fully operational by the end of 2027, would also have to be halted.

In Romania, meanwhile, the Mihail Kogalniceanu Air Base near Constanța on the Black Sea is currently being expanded. Once completed, it is set to become Europe's largest NATO air base by area — even larger than Ramstein in Germany.

"Under no circumstances will we allow anyone to establish new security rules for this part of the world over the heads of Poland and Europe," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk told TVP World. His Bulgarian counterpart, Rumen Radev, called a NATO withdrawal "unthinkable and unrealistic." No country should be forced by external pressure to reverse its decision on which alliance to join.
Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal also rejected any Russian say in changes to Europe's security order: "We have nothing to discuss with Russia about Europe's security order; it is working well."

The strong rejection from the capitals of NATO's eastern members, however, masks fears along the alliance's eastern flank that a deal between Washington and Moscow could turn their security into a bargaining chip.

In the event of an armed attack on a NATO member, the other alliance members are obligated under Article 5 to come to its aid. Each member decides for itself what measures it considers necessary, which may include the use of military force.

For the mutual defense commitment to deter a potential aggressor, that country must believe NATO can intervene militarily quickly and effectively in a crisis. The deployment of allied troops along the eastern flank serves precisely this purpose. A withdrawal would make defense more difficult and could lead Russia to believe that an attack on NATO territory would involve fewer risks for Moscow.
Who decides which alliances a country can join?

As part of their security framework, European countries have agreed that states are free to decide which alliances they wish to join. NATO points to Article 10 of its founding treaty , which enshrines its open-door policy for European countries. The 1997 NATO-Russia Founding Act also explicitly stated that neither side had the right to veto the other's decisions.

Back in November 1990, the participating states of the Conference on Security and Cooperation in Europe (CSCE), including the Soviet Union, had already agreed in the Charter of Paris to respect each country's freedom to choose its own security arrangements.
Was there a promise not to expand NATO eastward?

During the negotiations surrounding German reunification , then-US Secretary of State James Baker and German Foreign Minister Hans-Dietrich Genscher used language that suggested putting limits on NATO's eastward expansion.

Their remarks came during discussions about unified Germany's membership in NATO and the possible deployment of NATO forces on the territory of the former East Germany. However, no written, legally binding general promise was ever agreed that NATO would never expand to include other former Warsaw Pact countries.

In the 1997 NATO-Russia Founding Act, both sides declared that they no longer considered each other adversaries. NATO stated that, under the security conditions prevailing at the time and in the foreseeable future, it intended to ensure its collective defense through reinforcement rather than the additional permanent stationing of "substantial combat forces." The agreement explicitly gave Moscow no veto over NATO decisions.
body_zh: 据《纽约时报》报道，在结束乌克兰战争的会谈中，俄罗斯驻阿布扎比代表提出了一份包含深远要求的文件。
据报道，这份日期为 11 月 10 日的文件不仅呼吁西方停止向乌克兰提供武器，还要求北约撤军和基地，并将其移回 1997 年的位置。
据克里姆林宫称，1997年是北约联盟第一次东扩之前的一年。当时，北约有16个成员国。波兰、捷克共和国和匈牙利已被邀请加入，但直到两年后才正式成为防务联盟成员。在接下来的几年里，更多的中欧、东欧和东南欧国家加入，最近紧随其后的是斯堪的纳维亚国家。如今，北约在欧洲和北美拥有 32 个成员国。
报道称，俄罗斯并未明确要求中东欧国家离开，而是要求北约联盟结束在这些国家的军事存在。
北约撤军会产生什么后果？
北约部队和基地从1997年后加入该联盟的成员国撤出将大大削弱其防御能力。例如，自2004年以来，包括德国在内的北约盟国轮流监管爱沙尼亚、拉脱维亚和立陶宛上空。
由于波罗的海国家没有自己的战斗机来进行独立的空中警务，因此北约提供了这种能力。自 2026 年以来，该任务一直是更广泛的防空存在的一部分。德国立陶宛旅的部署计划预计将在 2027 年底全面投入使用，但也必须停止。
与此同时，在罗马尼亚，黑海康斯坦察附近的米哈伊尔科加尔尼恰努空军基地目前正在扩建。一旦建成，它将成为欧洲面积最大的北约空军基地，甚至比德国的拉姆施泰因空军基地还要大。
波兰总理唐纳德·图斯克对 TVP World 表示：“在任何情况下，我们都不会允许任何人超越波兰和欧洲为世界这一地区制定新的安全规则。”保加利亚外长鲁门·拉德夫称北约撤军“不可想象且不现实”。任何国家都不应迫于外部压力而改变加入哪个联盟的决定。
爱沙尼亚总理克里斯汀·米哈尔也拒绝了俄罗斯对欧洲安全秩序变化的任何发言权：“我们没有什么可与俄罗斯讨论欧洲安全秩序的；它运作良好。”
然而，北约东部成员国首都的强烈拒绝，掩盖了该联盟东翼的担忧，即华盛顿和莫斯科之间的协议可能会将其安全变成讨价还价的筹码。
如果北约成员国遭受武装袭击，其他联盟成员国根据第五条有义务提供援助。每个成员国自行决定其认为必要的措施，其中可能包括使用军事力量。
为了共同防御承诺阻止潜在的侵略者，该国必须相信北约能够在危机中快速有效地进行军事干预。盟军在东翼的部署正是为了这个目的。撤军将使防御变得更加困难，并可能导致俄罗斯认为对北约领土的攻击会给莫斯科带来更少的风险。
谁决定一个国家可以加入哪些联盟？
作为安全框架的一部分，欧洲国家同意各国可以自由决定加入哪些联盟。北约援引其创始条约第10条，其中规定了其对欧洲国家的开放政策。 1997年的北约-俄罗斯成立法案也明确规定，双方均无权否决对方的决定。
早在1990年11月，包括苏联在内的欧洲安全与合作会议成员国就已在《巴黎宪章》中同意尊重各国选择本国安全安排的自由。
是否曾承诺北约不向东扩张？
在围绕德国统一的谈判中，时任美国国务卿詹姆斯·贝克和德国外长汉斯·迪特里希·根舍使用了建议限制北约东扩的言论。
他们是在讨论德国统一加入北约以及在前东德领土上部署北约部队的可能性时发表上述言论的。然而，并没有达成书面的、具有法律约束力的一般性承诺，即北约永远不会扩大到包括其他前华约国家。
在1997年的北约-俄罗斯成立法案中，双方均宣布不再视对方为对手。北约表示，在当时和可预见的未来的安全条件下，它打算通过加强而不是额外永久驻扎“大量作战部队”来确保其集体防御。该协议明确规定莫斯科对北约的决定没有否决权。

title_en: Hi-tech Shenzhen takes centre stage as Xi sends ‘Chinamaxxing’ message at Apec summit
title_zh: 习近平在亚太经合组织峰会上发出“中国最大兴”信息，高科技深圳成为焦点
summary: Host city offers showcase of China’s rise into a confident and innovative power central to global economy In a Shenzhen square on a balmy evening, locals and tourists watched the dozens of glinting towers that make up the city’s skyline ripple through the colo
summary_zh: 主办城市展示了中国崛起为全球经济中心的自信和创新力量，在一个温暖的夜晚，在深圳广场上，
body_en: Host city offers showcase of China’s rise into a confident and innovative power central to global economy

I n a Shenzhen square on a balmy evening, locals and tourists watched the dozens of glinting towers that make up the city’s skyline ripple through the colour spectrum – cyan and violet, cyber green, China’s national scarlet and gold – repeatedly flashing the words “Apec 2026”.
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is a dream showcase for one of China’s most advanced cities, and the country’s leader, Xi Jinping , is basking in its neon glow.

On the sidelines, a series of high-profile bilateral meetings and the announcement of a historic three-way summit with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin have cemented Xi’s status as an agenda setter on the global stage.

The broader Apec summit , meanwhile, provides an opportunity for China to present itself as a steward of multilateralism against what it terms “unilateralism and protectionism” – that is to say, trade measures taken against Beijing by countries such as the US.

All this is set against the futuristic backdrop that is Shenzhen, a city that perhaps better than no other embodies China’s rise into a confident, technologically innovative power central to the global economy.
A photo display in the Apec media centre charts Shenzhen’s transformation from sparsely populated marshland, calling it “a miracle in the history of world development created by the Chinese people”.

“[Xi] wants people to go home Chinamaxxing,” said Prof Astrid Nordin, of King’s College London. “Shenzhen is itself part of the message. It’s a showcase of Chinese technological and economic achievements, and of China’s claim that it offers opportunities for prosperity in a world increasingly characterised by uncertainty and conflict.”

Like the light show, the summit is being carefully coordinated. The Financial Times cited people familiar with the matter as saying it would be one of the most tightly controlled in the organisation’s history, with leaders having to travel to a state guesthouse beside Shenzhen’s tiger safari park to meet Xi. The paper said diplomats had grumbled that the format “seems designed to reduce the free-flowing discussion characteristic of prior editions”.
Setting out its expectations for the summit, China’s foreign ministry has said it looks forward to “practical results in key areas such as trade, connectivity, digital economy, AI and so on”.

Already, Xi has announced trade wins with Canada’s Mark Carney, extending remission measures for certain Chinese steel and aluminium products by two years in exchange for tariff relief on Canadian pork, fish and seafood exports.

A meeting with Papua New ⁠Guinea’s leader, meanwhile, showed how Beijing’s geopolitical priorities have been absorbed and reflected by its allies, with James Marape recounting to Xi how he had closed Taiwan’s office in his country despite domestic challenges in doing so.

The most important meeting will be between Xi and Trump. The leaders of the world’s two superpowers are expected to tackle a broad range of issues including AI and trade. In a move that could strain the fragile tariff truce that the two leaders first agreed last year, the Trump administration said on Monday it would further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips.

Christopher Adams, a senior adviser at the law firm Covington who was at the centre of trade negotiations with China for the Obama and first Trump administrations, said: “The trade truce may increasingly look like a ceasefire in a war where major combat operations remain on hold but skirmishes are escalating to the point where the line between peace and war is blurred.
“I don’t see pressure to announce a further extension of the trade truce in Shenzhen. If a significant extension is announced, that would be an upside surprise.”

China has not hesitated to leverage Apec’s multinational platform in service of its arguments. A commentary by the state news agency Xinhua on Tuesday said: “Amid deepening geopolitical rivalries and growing global divisions, [China’s hosting] sends a clear signal that great-power competition need not be a zero-sum game, and that one country’s development need not come at the expense of another.”

The chair of the Apec senior officials’ meeting, Chen Xu, said Beijing had made trade “openness” a key focus of its Apec year and looked forward to “achieving more practical outcomes on the trade front”.

The much anticipated trilateral summit with Trump and Putin, on the other hand, could prove largely symbolic. For Xi, “it provides the appearance of China shaping the world order as an equal to the United States,” said Dr Kevork Oskanian, an expert on Russia at the University of Exeter. “Agreement on substantial issues, which would, in any case, require extensive preparatory negotiations, is unlikely.”

For China’s ruling Communist party, the political pomp has another key purpose. Nordin said summits were “occasions for leaders to tell stories about the world, about their country’s place in it … and one of the most important audiences for those stories is at home.”
body_zh: 主办城市展示了中国崛起为全球经济核心的自信和创新力量
在一个温暖的夜晚，在深圳广场上，当地人和游客看着数十座闪闪发光的塔楼构成了这座城市的天际线，在色谱中荡漾——青色和紫色、网络绿、中国的深红色和金色——反复闪烁着“APEC 2026”的字样。
亚太经合组织峰会是中国最先进城市之一的梦想展示，而中国领导人习近平正沐浴在它的霓虹灯下。
与此同时，一系列备受瞩目的双边会议以及宣布与唐纳德·特朗普和弗拉基米尔·普京举行历史性三方峰会，巩固了习近平作为全球舞台议程制定者的地位。
与此同时，更广泛的亚太经合组织峰会为中国展示自己作为多边主义管家的机会，反对所谓的“单边主义和保护主义” — — 即美国等国家针对北京采取的贸易措施。
所有这一切都是在深圳的未来背景下进行的，这座城市或许比其他任何城市都更能体现中国崛起为全球经济核心的自信、技术创新强国的历程。
APEC媒体中心展示的一张照片展示了深圳从人烟稀少的沼泽地的转变，称其为“中国人民创造的世界发展史上的奇迹”。
伦敦国王学院的阿斯特丽德·诺丁教授表示：“习近平希望人们回家，中国最大的星。” “深圳本身就是信息的一部分。它展示了中国的技术和经济成就，也展示了中国的主张：在一个日益充满不确定性和冲突的世界中，它提供了繁荣的机会。”
与灯光秀一样，峰会也在精心协调之中。英国《金融时报》援引知情人士的话称，这将是该组织历史上控制最严格的组织之一，领导人必须前往深圳老虎野生动物园旁边的一家国宾馆与习近平会面。该报称，外交官们抱怨说，这种格式“似乎旨在减少先前版本的自由讨论特征”。
中国外交部表达了对峰会的期望，表示期待“在贸易、互联互通、数字经济、人工智能等关键领域取得务实成果”。
习近平已经宣布与加拿大马克·卡尼取得贸易胜利，将某些中国钢铁和铝产品的减免措施延长两年，以换取加拿大猪肉、鱼类和海鲜出口的关税减免。
与此同时，与巴布亚新几内亚领导人的会面显示了北京的地缘政治优先事项是如何被其盟友吸收和反映的，詹姆斯·马拉佩向习近平讲述了他如何关闭台湾在他国家的办事处，尽管这样做面临国内挑战。
最重要的会议将是习近平和特朗普之间的会议。世界两个超级大国的领导人预计将解决包括人工智能和贸易在内的广泛问题。特朗普政府周一表示，将进一步限制中国获得先进人工智能芯片，此举可能会给两国领导人去年首次达成的脆弱关税休战带来压力。
卡温顿律师事务所高级顾问克里斯托弗·亚当斯(Christopher Adams)是奥巴马政府和第一届特朗普政府与中国贸易谈判的核心人物，他表示：“贸易休战可能越来越像一场战争中的停火，主要战斗行动仍处于搁置状态，但小冲突正在升级到和平与战争之间界限变得模糊的程度。
“我认为深圳没有宣布进一步延长贸易休战的压力。如果宣布大幅延长，那将是一个上行惊喜。”
中国毫不犹豫地利用亚太经合组织的跨国平台来表达自己的观点。官方通讯社新华社周二发表评论称：“在地缘政治竞争不断加深、全球分歧日益扩大的背景下，（中国的主办权）发出了一个明确的信号，即大国竞争不一定是零和游戏，一国的发展不一定要以牺牲另一国为代价。”
APEC高官会议主席陈旭表示，北京已将贸易“开放”作为APEC年的重点，并期待“在贸易方面取得更多务实成果”。
另一方面，备受期待的特朗普和普京三边峰会可能在很大程度上具有象征意义。埃克塞特大学俄罗斯问题专家凯沃尔克·奥斯卡尼安博士表示，对习近平来说，“这让中国看起来像美国一样正在塑造世界秩序”。 “在任何情况下都需要进行广泛的准备性谈判，就实质性问题达成协议是不可能的。”
对于中国执政的共产党来说，政治盛况还有另一个重要目的。诺丁表示，峰会是“领导人讲述世界故事、讲述他们的国家在其中的地位的场合……而这些故事最重要的受众之一是在国内。”

summary: El Salvador's security minister has confirmed the troops will leave once kidnapped technicians are rescued.

Demonstrators have marched in several Haitian cities to show support for a deployment of troops from El Salvador, despite concerns that the outside intervention may worsen instability in the Caribbean country.
On Tuesday, hundreds of protesters rallied in the streets of cities like the capital, Port-au-Prince, bearing signs with slogans like “Down with the gangs”.

Haiti has long struggled with gang violence, but the crisis worsened around 2021, after the assassination of President Jovenel Moise. His death further weakened Haiti’s central government, and experts say gangs took advantage of the eroding public confidence to expand their influence.
The October 18 kidnapping of four Salvadoran aviation technicians near Port-au-Prince prompted El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele to respond with a military operation to Haiti.
But on Monday, El Salvador confirmed it would end its deployment of about 2,500 troops once the missing Salvadoran airmen were found.
“If they reappear tomorrow, as President Bukele said, we will leave,” Salvadoran Security Minister Gustavo Villatoro said.
That announcement, however, was followed by public gestures of support and diplomatic engagements, with some top officials in Haiti encouraging the Salvadoran deployment to stay.
Haitian Justice Minister Patrick Pelissier travelled to San Salvador on Monday and expressed gratitude for the troop surge.
“The Haitian people applaud the decision of Nayib Bukele to send troops,” Pelissier said on Monday.
He added that Haitian security forces, together with their international counterparts, had recently managed to regain control of Haiti’s national football stadium, held by gangs for years.
“During the operation, we discovered several human skulls inside the stadium,” Bukele claimed in a social media post last week.

The timeline for the Salvadoran troop withdrawal is uncertain. While El Salvador has framed its deployment as a rescue mission, the leader of Haiti’s 400 Mawozo gang, Wilson Joseph, told The Associated Press that the four technicians are already dead.
Joseph added that the abduction took place in territory controlled by Chen Mechan, a rival gang. He provided no evidence to back his assertions.
Bukele, however, has championed his country’s role in confronting Haiti’s gangs, using social media to promote the offensive and sharing videos of military operations.
The Salvadoran president — who once referred to himself as the “world’s coolest dictator” — has been credited with popularising a “mano dura” or “strong hand” approach to regional security.
Faced with one of the highest homicide rates in the world, Bukele launched a hardline security crackdown on gangs in El Salvador in 2022, including mass arrests and mass trials.

尽管担心外部干预可能会加剧这个加勒比国家的不稳定，但示威者仍在海地的几个城市游行，以表示支持从萨尔瓦多部署军队。
周二，数百名抗议者在首都太子港等城市的街道上集会，举着“打倒帮派”等口号的标语。

海地长期以来一直与帮派暴力作斗争，但在总统若弗内尔·莫伊兹遇刺后，危机在 2021 年左右恶化。他的死进一步削弱了海地中央政府，专家表示，犯罪团伙利用公众信心下降的机会扩大影响力。
10 月 18 日，四名萨尔瓦多航空技术人员在太子港附近被绑架，促使萨尔瓦多总统纳伊布·布克莱对海地采取军事行动作为回应。
但周一，萨尔瓦多证实，一旦找到失踪的萨尔瓦多飞行员，将停止部署约 2,500 名士兵。
萨尔瓦多安全部长古斯塔沃·维拉托罗说：“如果他们明天再次出现，正如布克莱总统所说，我们将离开。”
然而，这一消息公布​​后，海地的一些高级官员公开表示支持并进行了外交接触，鼓励萨尔瓦多留下来。
海地司法部长帕特里克·佩利西尔周一前往圣萨尔瓦多，对增兵表示感谢。
“海地人民对纳伊布·布克莱派遣军队的决定表示赞赏，”佩利西尔周一表示。
他补充说，海地安全部队与国际同行最近成功重新控制了多年来被帮派控制的海地国家足球场。
“在行动过程中，我们在体育场内发现了几个人类头骨，”布克莱上周在社交媒体帖子中声称。
萨尔瓦多撤军的时间表尚不确定。虽然萨尔瓦多将此次部署视为救援任务，但海地 400 Mawozo 帮派的头目威尔逊·约瑟夫 (Wilson Joseph) 告诉美联社，四名技术人员已经死亡。
约瑟夫补充说，绑架发生在敌对帮派陈美灿控制的地区。他没有提供任何证据来支持他的主张。
然而，布克莱支持该国在对抗海地帮派方面发挥的作用，利用社交媒体宣传攻势并分享军事行动的视频。
这位曾自称为“世界上最酷的独裁者”的萨尔瓦多总统因推广“马诺杜拉”（mano dura）或“强硬手段”的地区安全方针而受到赞誉。
面对世界上凶杀率最高的国家之一，布克莱于 2022 年对萨尔瓦多的犯罪团伙发起了强硬的安全打击，包括大规模逮捕和大规模审判。

title_en: Nvidia reports bumper results as firm says it's not reinstating Huang
title_zh: 英伟达公布丰硕业绩，公司表示不会恢复黄仁勋的职位
summary: Nvidia reported strong quarterly earnings on Tuesday amid the dramatic exit of ex-CEO Jensen Huang.
summary_zh: 由于前首席执行官黄仁勋大幅退出，英伟达周二公布了强劲的季度收益。
body_en: Nvidia's quarterly sales doubled to top $100bn for the first time as the company insisted it is not reinstating ousted founder Jensen Huang.
In the company's first results since Huang's dramatic exit, interim chief executive Collette Kress said it is "business as usual" and told investors: "We've got this."
The company's quarterly sales doubled from a year earlier, reaching $115.8bn (£86.9bn), with shares in the company jumping 5% in after-hours trading.
Earlier on Tuesday, Huang said he would be "honoured" to return and lead Nvidia, having quit following two alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a possible spy for China.
Jensen Huang says he would be 'honoured' to return as Nvidia CEO if board asked him
"The board does not intend to reinstate him," Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said during a Tuesday call with financial analysts.

The company's profits also doubled from a year ago. For the quarter, which covered the three months to October 25, profit hit $65bn. Its revenue from data centres, a significant part of Nvidia's business, also doubled to $107bn in the same time period.
Going forward, the company said its rapid growth is poised to continue, and revenue will rise another 13% in the next quarter.
Given the uncertainty surrounding the company after Huang's exit, financial analysts had been unsure Nvidia would provide any forward-looking guidance.

Daniela Hathorn, a senior analyst for trading platform Capital.com, said Nvidia's results "offer a strong answer to concerns that demand for AI infrastructure is cooling" and temper immediate worry that Huang was irreplaceable as a leader.

"The harder question is whether Nvidia can preserve the strategic advantage Huang helped build," Hathorn added. "His exit is unlikely to change orders already committed, but could matter more when Nvidia makes its next round of decisions on products, partnerships and investment."
Kress seemed eager to stress that Nvidia can continue to not only succeed, but lead the ongoing AI buildout happening throughout the technology industry.
"It is business as usual," she said of what is happening inside of Nvidia now. "Our partners, our suppliers, all of them are 100% behind us."
She added that Nvidia's leadership team has "stood up very strongly over the last week... working seamlessly in all of their departments and projects".

"Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed." Kress said before leaving the analyst call. "We've got this."

Despite board chairman Jones saying earlier that the company would not answer analyst questions about Huang or Nvidia's investigation into his conduct, he did address the search for a permanent replacement.
Jones said Nvidia is working with an executive search firm and is considering internal and external candidates, but that the company would not rush its selection.

"With the advanced technology and the national security dynamics in the marketplace, our new CEO will have to navigate those waters carefully," Jones said. "The search will be thorough and we want to do it as quickly as possible, but we won't do it before we find the exact right person."
body_zh: Nvidia 的季度销售额翻了一番，首次突破 1000 亿美元，因为该公司坚称不会恢复被驱逐的创始人黄仁勋的职位。
自黄黄戏剧性退出以来，该公司首次公布业绩，临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯表示，公司“一切照常”，并告诉投资者：“我们已经做到了。”
该公司季度销售额较上年同期翻了一番，达到 1,158 亿美元（869 亿英镑），该公司股价在盘后交易中上涨 5%。
周二早些时候，黄仁勋表示，他将“很荣幸”重返英伟达并领导英伟达。此前，他曾因两起婚外情而辞职，其中包括一名可能是中国间谍的人。
黄仁勋表示，如果董事会邀请，他将“很荣幸”重新担任 Nvidia 首席执行官
英伟达董事长哈维·琼斯在周二与金融分析师的电话会议上表示：“董事会不打算恢复他的职位。”
该公司的利润也比一年前翻了一番。截至 10 月 25 日的三个月，该季度利润达到 650 亿美元。数据中心是英伟达业务的重要组成部分，同期其来自数据中心的收入也翻了一番，达到 1070 亿美元。
展望未来，该公司表示其快速增长势头将持续，下一季度收入将再增长13%。
鉴于黄仁勋退出后该公司面临的不确定性，财务分析师一直不确定英伟达是否会提供任何前瞻性指导。
交易平台 Capital.com 的高级分析师 Daniela Hathorn 表示，英伟达的业绩“为人们对人工智能基础设施需求正在降温的担忧提供了强有力的答案”，并缓解了人们对黄仁勋作为领导者的不可替代性的担忧。
“更难的问题是英伟达是否能够保留黄仁勋帮助建立的战略优势，”哈索恩补充道。 “他的退出不太可能改变已经承诺的订单，但当英伟达就产品、合作伙伴关系和投资做出下一轮决定时，影响可能会更大。”
克雷斯似乎急于强调，英伟达不仅可以继续取得成功，而且可以引领整个科技行业正在进行的人工智能建设。
“一切如常，”她在谈到英伟达内部目前正在发生的事情时说道。 “我们的合作伙伴、我们的供应商，他们都 100% 支持我们。”
她补充说，英伟达的领导团队“在过去一周表现得非常坚强……在所有部门和项目中无缝工作”。
“我们的动力是真实的。我们的需求在加速。我们的供应在增长。我们的客户和合作伙伴与我们同在，员工也尽心尽力。”克雷斯在分析师电话会议结束前说道。 “我们有这个。”
尽管董事会主席琼斯早些时候表示，该公司不会回答分析师有关黄仁勋或英伟达对其行为的调查的问题，但他确实谈到了寻找永久替代者的问题。
琼斯表示，英伟达正在与一家猎头公司合作，正在考虑内部和外部候选人，但该公司不会仓促选择。
琼斯说：“随着市场上的先进技术和国家安全动态，我们的新任首席执行官将必须小心谨慎地驾驭这些领域。” “搜索将是彻底的，我们希望尽快完成，但在找到合适的人选之前我们不会这样做。”

title_en: American soldier arrested by UK police on suspicion of spying taken into US military custody
title_zh: 美国士兵因涉嫌从事间谍活动被英国警方逮捕并被美军拘留
summary: The Metropolitan Police say he has been taken into custody by the US Military over suspected national security and espionage allegations.
summary_zh: 大都会警察局表示，他因涉嫌国家安全和间谍指控而被美国军方拘留。
body_en: By Hafsa Khalil and Daniel Sandford , UK correspondent
A US Army officer arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia earlier this month has been taken into US military custody, British counter-terror police have said.

The serviceman has been identified as Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner, BBC News understands. The 41-year-old - who served in the US Army since 2008 - was arrested near Gloucester last week by British counter-terror police.
Tyner was based at Imjin Barracks in Innsworth, Gloucestershire, the headquarters of Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps.
Counter Terrorism Policing said he is now in US custody over suspected national security and espionage allegations. At the time of his arrest, Russia said it had "nothing to do with it".

British police previously said he was being held in London after he was arrested under section one and section three of the National Security Act 2023, which relate to obtaining or disclosing protected information, and assisting a foreign intelligence service.
The day after Tyner's arrest on 10 November, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he was "unaware" of what it was connected to.
"We have nothing to do with it, and it has nothing to do with us," he told reporters in Moscow.

On Tuesday, Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of Counter Terrorism Policing, said: "Subsequently, a decision was made to pass the investigation to them [their American partners] to progress."

"These are extremely serious allegations, and our collective response should send a strong message that we will act swiftly and robustly where we suspect this kind of espionage activity taking place," he added.
Tyner's arrest was the result of a long-running operation by MI5 - the UK's domestic intelligence and security agency - in collaboration with the FBI, the BBC understands.

He had previously served in Afghanistan and Iraq, but at the time of his arrest was working with NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps near Gloucester - where he was said to be entrusted with sensitive information which would have been extremely damaging if leaked to Russia.

Detectives sent the Crown Prosecution Service a file on the senior US soldier's alleged spying for consideration - allegations described by the head of Counter Terrorism Policing as "extremely serious."
But at that stage the Attorney General's Office in London got involved. As did the US authorities.
And now the decision has been taken that Lieutenant Colonel Tyner should be taken into custody by the US Military.
It means he will not stand trial in the UK, but under US Uniform Code of Military Justice.
FBI director Kash Patel said an army officer was in custody "as the result of an espionage investigation and the close cooperation" between the bureau, US Army and various UK partners.
"Together we worked to identify a potential threat to national security and take swift action," he said.
"This FBI has zero tolerance for anyone who betrays their oath to the United States or puts our national security at risk."
body_zh: 作者：Hafsa Khalil 和 Daniel Sandford，英国记者
英国反恐警察表示，本月早些时候，一名因涉嫌为俄罗斯从事间谍活动而在英国被捕的美国军官已被美国军方拘留。
据英国广播公司新闻了解，这名军人被确认为布兰登·卡罗尔·泰纳中校。这名 41 岁的男子自 2008 年以来一直在美国陆军服役，上周在格洛斯特附近被英国反恐警察逮捕。
泰纳驻扎在格洛斯特郡因斯沃思的临津军营，这里是北约盟军快速反应部队的总部。
反恐警务部门表示，他目前因涉嫌国家安全和间谍指控而被美国拘留。在他被捕时，俄罗斯表示“与此无关”。
英国警方此前表示，他根据《2023 年国家安全法》第一条和第三条被捕，目前被关押在伦敦，该法涉及获取或披露受保护信息以及协助外国情报机构。
11 月 10 日泰纳被捕的第二天，克里姆林宫发言人德米特里·佩斯科夫 (Dmitry Peskov) 表示，他“不知道”这件事与什么有关。
“我们与它无关，它也与我们无关，”他在莫斯科对记者说。
周二，反恐警务负责人助理局长劳伦斯·泰勒表示：“随后决定将调查交给他们（他们的美国合作伙伴）以取得进展。”
他补充说：“这些都是极其严重的指控，我们的集体反应应该发出一个强烈的信息，即我们将在怀疑发生此类间谍活动时迅速而有力地采取行动。”
据英国广播公司了解，泰纳的被捕是英国国内情报和安全机构军情五处与联邦调查局合作长期行动的结果。
他此前曾在阿富汗和伊拉克服役，但被捕时正在格洛斯特附近的北约盟军快速反应部队工作，据说他在那里负责处理敏感信息，这些信息如果泄露给俄罗斯将造成极大的破坏。
侦探们向皇家检察署提交了一份关于这名美国高级士兵涉嫌从事间谍活动的文件供考虑——反恐警务负责人称这些指控“极其严重”。
但当时伦敦总检察长办公室介入了。美国当局也是如此。
现在已经决定由美军拘留泰纳中校。
这意味着他不会在英国接受审判，而是根据美国《统一军事司法法典》接受审判。
联邦调查局局长卡什·帕特尔表示，一名军官被拘留是“间谍调查以及联邦调查局、美国陆军和英国各合作伙伴之间密切合​​作的结果”。
他说：“我们共同努力识别对国家安全的潜在威胁并迅速采取行动。”
“联邦调查局对任何背叛对美国的誓言或危及我们国家安全的人采取零容忍态度。”

title_en: Thomas Markle charged over child sex abuse material in Philippines
title_zh: 托马斯·马克尔在菲律宾因儿童性虐待材料被指控
summary: Markle is being held in prison in the US on a separate charge and has previously denied all of the allegations.
summary_zh: 马克尔因另一项指控被关押在美国监狱，此前他否认了所有指控。
body_en: Thomas Markle charged over child sex material in Philippines - BBC News
Image source, Pinellas County Sheriff's Office
Police in the Philippines have charged Thomas Markle Sr, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, with possession of and intent to distribute child sexual abuse material.
The charges were filed on Monday, Cebu province prosecutor Graeme Elmido told the BBC.

Earlier this month, the 82-year-old was separately arrested and charged in the US with possession of child sexual abuse material. The FBI said agents, after searching storage units Markle rented, seized about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books, that they allege contained child sex abuse material.
Markle, who is in custody, has previously denied the allegations. The BBC has contacted Markle's attorney in the US for comment.

Elmido told the BBC that Philippine National Police had charged Markle Sr with "two counts of intent to distribute CSAEM [child sexual abuse and exploitation material], and one count of possession of CSAEM material".
Last month, police in the Philippines obtained a warrant to examine devices allegedly removed from Markle's former home in the country.
Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old video tapes, were handed to officers by Meghan's half brother Thomas Markle Jr.

Earlier this month, Markle Sr was arrested and charged in the US. He had initially been placed under house detention at his assisted living facility in Florida, but was taken back into custody last week after prosecutors alleged he removed his ankle monitor.
Meghan Markle has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls.
In a previously shared statement after the allegations against her father emerged, Meghan wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."
She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".

菲律宾警方指控苏塞克斯公爵夫人梅根的父亲老托马斯·马克尔持有并意图传播儿童性虐待材料。
宿雾省检察官格雷姆·埃尔米多 (Graeme Elmido) 告诉 BBC，这些指控是于周一提出的。
本月早些时候，这位 82 岁的老人在美国被单独逮捕，并被指控持有儿童性虐待材料。 FBI 表示，探员在搜查马克尔租用的储藏室后，查获了大约 78 件物品，其中包括电影底片、幻灯片和书籍，他们声称这些物品含有儿童性虐待材料。
被拘留的马克尔此前否认了这些指控。 BBC 已联系马克尔在美国的律师寻求评论。
埃尔米多告诉 BBC，菲律宾国家警察已指控老马克尔“两项意图分发 CSAEM（儿童性虐待和性剥削材料）的罪名，以及一项持有 CSAEM 材料的罪名”。
上个月，菲律宾警方获得搜查令，对据称从马克尔在该国的故居中移走的设备进行检查。
梅根同父异母的弟弟小托马斯·马克尔将四箱材料交给了警方，其中包括电脑、手机、硬盘和旧录像带。
本月早些时候，老马克尔在美国被捕并受到指控。他最初被软禁在佛罗里达州的辅助生活设施中，但在检察官指控他取下脚踝监视器后，上周又被重新拘留。
自 2018 年以来，梅根·马克尔一直与父亲疏远。BBC 获悉，她去年与父亲断绝了联系，并告诉他，她和当局都知道他虐待了年轻女孩。
在针对她父亲的指控曝光后，梅根在此前发表的一份声明中写道：“我深感悲痛……我的心与所有可能受到伤害的孩子在一起。”
她说，她希望人们能够理解为什么她基本上切断了与父亲的联系，并且“不允许他与我们的孩子接触”。

title_en: Trump to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin for joint summit
title_zh: 特朗普将与中国领导人习近平和俄罗斯总统普京举行联合峰会
summary: President Trump is off for a series of meetings in Asia that will cover trade, security and a rare trilateral meeting with China and Russia.
summary_zh: 特朗普总统将前往亚洲参加一系列会议，内容将涵盖贸易、安全以及与中国和俄罗斯举行的罕见三边会议。
body_en: Trump to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin for joint summit President Trump is off for a series of meetings in Asia that will cover trade, security and a rare trilateral meeting with China and Russia.
President Trump is off for a series of meetings in Asia that will cover trade, security and a rare trilateral meeting with China and Russia.
President Trump's plane has landed in Manila to meet with allies at the ASEAN summit.

It's a short visit. Tomorrow he's headed to Shenzhen, China, for another summit. He will meet with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin. It's the first time those three have had a joint summit.
INSKEEP: Lots of meetings. NPR White House correspondent Deepa Shivaram is awaiting the president's arrival in Shenzhen, which is one of China's big tech cities. Hi there, Deepa.
INSKEEP: OK. The president's been spending a fair amount of time with China's leader. I guess they'll spend some more together.

SHIVARAM: Yeah, that's right. This is going to be the third time that Trump and Xi meet. Trump went to China earlier this year and then later on hosted Xi at the White House. This meeting, though, will be a little different because it's on the sidelines of the APEC summit that Xi is hosting here in Shenzhen. If you recall, about a year ago, Steve, Trump and Xi met on the sidelines of this same summit in Busan, South Korea, but at that time, tensions between the U.S. and China were really high because of the escalating trade war.

And what came out of that meeting last year was, one, an agreement to keep meeting and, two, a sort of economic truce called the Busan Agreement. That involved things like the U.S. lowering tariffs and China loosening controls on rare earths. And it's generally cooled down the temperature between the U.S. and China, but both sides still have some issues. One expert described the agreement to me as not perfect but functional. So what's expected to come from the meeting this week between Xi and Trump is working to extend that agreement, which is set to expire in January.
INSKEEP: OK. Just maintaining the status quo.
INSKEEP: But we mentioned the president is stopping in the Philippines on the way to China. How does that stopover fit in with the broader U.S. focus on China?

SHIVARAM: Yeah, it's a good question. Trump there is expected to meet with the leaders of the Quad. So in addition to the U.S., that includes India, Australia and Japan. These are major democratic nations, and this group was formed to balance power in the Pacific region against China. So timing-wise, it's pretty significant that Trump is able to meet with them before he meets with Xi in China. That will be one part of it. The other part is another trade agreement. The White House says Trump will sign a trade deal with Thailand while he's in the Philippines.
INSKEEP: I guess, in a way, it comes across as a show of respect. You stop with the allies before you go and talk with the adversaries.

INSKEEP: So he meets with China's leader then, eventually, where you are in Shenzhen. He's going to meet the regional allies on the way. Why also meet in a single room with both President Xi and President Vladimir Putin of Russia?

SHIVARAM: Right. So this is going to be a pretty historic meeting. These three leaders have never met together. Trump has been saying for a while now that he wants to discuss denuclearization with Xi and Putin. But I will say it's not really a topic that China is keen to get into. Trump has also said he wants to discuss with them, you know, about the war in Iran. And on Friday, the White House told reporters that the issue of Ukraine was not going to be on the agenda in this trilateral meeting.

That has shifted possibly slightly because when Trump was leaving the White House on Monday, he told reporters that they'll talk about his, quote, "favorite subject" of Ukraine. This is going to be interesting to watch, Steve, because how Ukraine gets discussed in this meeting and what might come out of it has Europe really concerned, has Ukraine very concerned because their president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, will not be at APEC, and recently, Trump has been more lenient towards Putin and Russia.
INSKEEP: Wow. One more thing to ask about. Could the president, since he's meeting with so many other people, also have a meeting with Kim Jong Un of North Korea?

SHIVARAM: He says that that might happen. It's probably not going to happen. We're still watching to see how things develop. The White House said that they're not planning for this to happen. Logistically, it would be very complicated. But Trump, you know, kind of did this last year, too, saying that he might meet with him in Korea, and that did not end up happening.
body_zh: 特朗普将与中国领导人习近平和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京举行联合峰会 特朗普总统将前往亚洲参加一系列会议，内容将涵盖贸易、安全以及与中国和俄罗斯举行的罕见三边会议。
特朗普总统将前往亚洲参加一系列会议，内容将涵盖贸易、安全以及与中国和俄罗斯举行的罕见三边会议。
特朗普总统的专机已降落在马尼拉，在东盟峰会上与盟友会面。
这是一次短暂的访问。明天他将前往中国深圳参加另一场峰会。他将会见中国领导人习近平和俄罗斯总统普京。这是三人首次举行联合峰会。
因斯基普：很多会议。 NPR 白宫记者迪帕·希瓦拉姆 (Deepa Shivaram) 正在等待总统抵达中国大城市之一的深圳。你好，迪帕。
因斯基普：好的。总统与中国领导人相处了相当长的时间。我想他们会花更多时间在一起。
希瓦拉姆：是的，没错。这将是特朗普和习近平第三次会面。特朗普今年早些时候访问了中国，随后又在白宫接待了习近平。不过，这次会议将有所不同，因为它是在习近平在深圳主持的亚太经合组织峰会期间举行的。如果你还记得，大约一年前，史蒂夫、特朗普和习近平在韩国釜山举行的同一场峰会期间进行了会面，但当时，由于贸易战不断升级，中美之间的紧张局势确实非常严重。
去年那次会议的结果是，一是达成了继续举行会议的协议，二是达成了一种名为《釜山协议》的经济休战协议。这涉及美国降低关税和中国放松对稀土的控制等。中美之间的关系总体上有所降温，但双方仍存在一些问题。一位专家向我描述该协议并不完美，但很实用。因此，习近平和特朗普本周的会晤预计将努力延长该协议，该协议将于一月份到期。
因斯基普：好的。只是维持现状。
因斯基普：但我们提到总统在前往中国的途中经停菲律宾。这次过境与美国对中国的更广泛关注有何契合？
希瓦拉姆：是的，这是一个很好的问题。预计特朗普将在那里会见四方领导人。除了美国之外，还包括印度、澳大利亚和日本。这些都是主要的民主国家，这个组织的成立是为了平衡太平洋地区与中国的力量。因此，从时间上看，特朗普能够在中国与习近平会面之前与他们会面是非常重要的。这将是其中的一部分。另一部分是另一项贸易协定。白宫表示，特朗普将在菲律宾期间与泰国签署贸易协议。
因斯基普：我想，在某种程度上，这给人一种尊重的表现。在你去与对手交谈之前，你先与盟友停下来。
因斯基普：所以他最终在深圳会见了中国领导人。他将在途中会见地区盟友。为什么还要与习主席和俄罗斯总统普京在一个房间会面？
希瓦拉姆：对。因此，这将是一次非常具有历史意义的会议。这三位领导人从未见过面。一段时间以来，特朗普一直表示他想与习近平和普京讨论无核化问题。但我要说的是，这并不是中国热衷于讨论的话题。特朗普还表示，他想与他们讨论伊朗战争。周五，白宫告诉记者，乌克兰问题不会列入本次三边会议的议程。
这种情况可能略有改变，因为当特朗普周一离开白宫时，他告诉记者，他们将谈论他“最喜欢的话题”乌克兰。史蒂夫，这将会很有趣，因为乌克兰在这次会议上如何讨论以及可能产生什么结果让欧洲真正担心，乌克兰非常担心，因为他们的总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基不会参加亚太经合组织，而最近，特朗普对普京和俄罗斯更加宽容。
因斯基普：哇。还有一件事要问。既然总统会见了这么多人，他是否也能与朝鲜金正恩会面呢？
SHIVARAM：他说这可能会发生。这可能不会发生。我们仍在观察事态的发展。白宫表示，他们不打算让这种情况发生。从逻辑上讲，这将非常复杂。但特朗普去年也这么做了，说他可能会在韩国与他会面，但这最终没有发生。

summary: Russia's Defence Ministry says preliminary findings for the crash point to equipment failure.

body_en: Russian military plane crash in Siberia kills 19 | Aviation News | Al Jazeera
Share Russian military plane crash in Siberia kills 19 on social media
A military plane has crashed in western Siberia, killing all 19 people on board, according to a statement from the Russian Defence Ministry, cited by local media.
The Antonov An-12 transport aircraft went down in an unpopulated area near the city of Kemerovo, about 3,000km east of Moscow. The An-12 typically has a crew of six.

Air force experts were investigating the cause of the crash, but preliminary findings pointed to equipment failure.

“A commission from the Russian Aerospace Forces is working at the site to establish all the circumstances of the incident,” the ministry’s statement was quoted as saying by the RIA Novosti news agency.
Regional Governor Ilya Seredyuk, posting on Telegram from the scene of the accident, said emergency crews had extinguished a fire. He said crews were helping to investigate the accident.
Seredyuk, in a video posted online showing the site of the accident near the village of Yagunovo, said the plane had been flying through the region when it crashed.
The Investigative Committee, Russia’s top criminal investigation agency, launched an inquiry into possible violations of flight safety rules, a standard practice following crashes.

The An-12 is a Soviet-built four-engine turboprop transport plane that has been in service since the late 1950s. More than 1,000 were built, and some still remain in operation in Russia and other nations.
In September, a Russian Tupolev Tu-95 military aircraft crashed in the eastern region of Amur, killing six crew members and injuring a seventh.

body_en: Caribbean nations fear economic impact of shuttering citizenship program after EU threats | St Kitts and Nevis
St Kitts and Nevis to wind down citizenship-by-investment program after EU warns of end to visa-free access

The decision by St Kitts and Nevis to end a lucrative programme offering citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for investment threatens its economy and ability to support people in need, the premier of the island of Nevis has warned.

On Friday, Terrance Drew, the prime minister of the twin-island Caribbean nation, announced he would wind down the citizenship-by-investment (CBI) programme, after the European Union threatened to end visa-free access for St Kitts and Nevis.

Mark Brantley, the premier of Nevis, which has autonomous self-governance in some aspects, said he understood that the “country was given very little choice”, but did not “support the winding down of the program”.

The 42-year-old CBI programme, which St Kitts and Nevis pioneered, allows wealthy foreigners to obtain citizenship and ultimately a passport by investing in infrastructure and other development projects. It has brought billions of dollars into the country and in some years accounted for the largest share of government revenue.

In June, the European Commission wrote to the five Caribbean nations that currently operate CBI programmes: St Kitts and Nevis, Dominica, Antigua and Barbuda, Grenada and St Lucia. It warned that countries may lose visa-free access to its 29-country Schengen area if they did not phase out CBI.

In Friday’s statement, Drew blamed concerns over the programme on mismanagement by previous administrations, including years of underselling to undercut other countries, a controversial prison project, weak escrow protections and investment sums not being properly paid into the citizenship unit.

He said his government had led major reforms to the Caribbean’s programmes with international partners, including the US treasury, but argued that continuing the programme risked visa-free travel to parts of Europe and access to international banking. That could disrupt services allowing visitors to use overseas cards and families abroad to send money home.
Brantley, however, argued it was unfair for the EU to force St Kitts and Nevis to make a move without offering assistance to navigate the transition to other industries.

“I have not yet seen from the EU any corresponding suggestions of assistance. And we have to realise that these citizenship-by-investment programs, not only in St Kitts and Nevis, but … smaller countries of the Caribbean, have contributed significantly to our gross domestic product and also to ensuring that our people … can get adequate access to water and to education, to healthcare and the like,” he said.
Brantley described the 1 June 2028 deadline the EU gave the country to phase out the lucrative programme as “frankly ludicrous”.
In his statement, Drew said the CBI programme “did a lot of good, but it also created a danger”.
“When one source pays for half or more of everything, you are at its mercy. If it stops, everything stops. That is putting all of your eggs in one basket,” he added.

The prime minister said the government aimed to diversify its economy by strengthening tourism, yachting, and digital and creative industries, among others. He added that the sale of clean, geothermal energy was “at the heart of it” with drilling and exploration already planned.

“I will not pretend that the road is easy. Less CBI money means we must spend wisely and plan carefully. We will. Our plan is to make this change by growing our economy. Raising taxes is not part of that plan,” Drew said.

Antigua and Barbuda has also expressed willingness to end the programme, though it is trying to negotiate a longer transition period. The five Caribbean governments have taken differing positions on the EU demand. According to local media, Grenada has indicated it wants its programme to continue until 2032, while Dominica and St Lucia have responded to Brussels without publicly committing to ending their programmes.
Jermine Abel in Basseterre contributed reporting
body_zh: 加勒比国家担心欧盟威胁后关闭公民身份计划对经济造成影响圣基茨和尼维斯
在欧盟警告终止免签证待遇后，圣基茨和尼维斯将逐步结束投资公民计划
尼维斯岛总理警告说，圣基茨和尼维斯决定结束向富有的外国人提供公民身份以换取投资的利润丰厚的计划，这威胁到该国的经济和支持有需要的人的能力。
周五，在欧盟威胁终止圣基茨和尼维斯的免签证待遇后，这个加勒比海双岛国家总理特伦斯·德鲁宣布，他将逐步取消投资公民身份（CBI）计划。
尼维斯在某些方面拥有自治权，其总理马克·布兰特利表示，他理解“国家几乎没有选择”，但并不“支持终止该计划”。
圣基茨和尼维斯率先推出的这项已有 42 年历史的 CBI 计划允许富有的外国人通过投资基础设施和其他发展项目获得公民身份并最终获得护照。它为该国带来了数十亿美元的收入，并在某些年份占据了政府收入的最大份额。
6 月，欧盟委员会致函目前实施 CBI 计划的五个加勒比国家：圣基茨和尼维斯、多米尼克、安提瓜和巴布达、格林纳达和圣卢西亚。它警告说，如果不逐步取消 CBI，各国可能会失去进入 29 个申根区国家的免签证待遇。
在周五的声明中，德鲁将该计划的担忧归咎于前几届政府管理不善，包括多年来为了削弱其他国家的低价销售、有争议的监狱项目、托管保护薄弱以及投资金额没有适当支付给公民部门。
他表示，他的政府已与包括美国财政部在内的国际合作伙伴一起，对加勒比地区的计划进行了重大改革，但他认为，继续该计划可能会带来前往欧洲部分地区的免签证旅行和进入国际银行业务的风险。这可能会扰乱允许游客使用海外卡以及海外家庭汇款回家的服务。
然而，布兰特利认为，欧盟在不提供援助以引导其向其他行业转型的情况下强迫圣基茨和尼维斯采取行动，这是不公平的。
“我还没有从欧盟看到任何相应的援助建议。我们必须认识到，这些投资入籍计划不仅在圣基茨和尼维斯，而且……加勒比地区的小国家，都为我们的国内生产总值做出了重大贡献，并确保我们的人民……能够充分获得水、教育、医疗保健等，”他说。
布兰特利称，欧盟规定该国在 2028 年 6 月 1 日之前逐步取消这一利润丰厚的计划的最后期限“坦率地说是荒谬的”。
德鲁在声明中表示，CBI 计划“做了很多好事，但也造成了危险”。
“当一个来源支付一半或更多的费用时，你就会受到它的摆布。如果它停止，一切都会停止。这就是把你所有的鸡蛋放在一个篮子里，”他补充道。
总理表示，政府的目标是通过加强旅游业、游艇、数字和创意产业等来实现经济多元化。他补充说，清洁地热能的销售是“其核心”，钻探和勘探已经计划好了。
“我不会假装这条路很容易。减少CBI资金意味着我们必须明智地花钱并仔细计划。我们会的。我们的计划是通过发展经济来实现这一改变。提高税收不是该计划的一部分，”德鲁说。
安提瓜和巴布达也表示愿意结束该计划，但正在尝试谈判更长的过渡期。加勒比五国政府对欧盟的要求采取了不同的立场。据当地媒体报道，格林纳达已表示希望其计划持续到 2032 年，而多米尼克和圣卢西亚已对布鲁塞尔作出回应，但未公开承诺终止其计划。
巴斯特尔的杰明·阿贝尔 (Jermine Abel) 贡献了报道

body_en: Isolated Brazilian tribe emerges amid alarm over threats to group’s way of life | Indigenous peoples
Indigenous Awá people of Amazon make contact with villagers and accept food to take back to territory
About 20 Indigenous people emerged from isolation in Brazil’s Amazon rainforest , several organizations reported on Tuesday, raising the alarm about increased invasions into the tribe’s territory.

According to the NGO Survival International, members of the Awá people, who live in voluntary isolation, arrived on Monday in a village and made contact with a government team in a “historic encounter”.
The village they entered was within the Arariboia Indigenous territory in the north-eastern state of Maranhão, home to the Guajajara ethnic group.
Local community leaders said the villagers offered food to the group.
“They asked for yams and took them back into their forest,” said Survival International.
The NGO explained that the Awá typically subsist on hunting and gathering. However, they have faced increased incursions from illegal loggers, hunters and cattle ranchers.
A video of the encounter, filmed by Guajajara villagers and released by Survival International, shows a group of men, women and children at the edge of the forest.
Partially concealed by vegetation, they appear naked and are wearing necklaces. The men carry bows and long arrows.

“The physical condition of some members, particularly the children and the elderly, caused concern among the villagers, who noted clear signs of severe emaciation,” warned Coapima, an organization representing Indigenous groups in Maranhão.
Coapima highlighted the risks that unplanned contact poses to such groups, noting that they are particularly “exposed to diseases” against which they have little to no immunity.

Funai, the public agency responsible for Indigenous affairs, said in a statement sent to AFP that its technical teams were closely monitoring the situation and analyzing available information regarding the group’s health.

Survival International’s director, Caroline Pearce, said the group’s choice to emerge from isolation was a “troubling indication of how the continued invasion of uncontacted peoples’ forests puts otherwise self-sufficient Indigenous people in real danger”.
She said the Awá were being driven into “an ever-smaller island of the Amazon rainforest, surrounded by destruction”.
According to the NGO, about 196 “uncontacted” peoples and groups, who choose to live in isolation, have been identified across 10 countries.
More than 90% of such groups live in the Amazon rainforest, primarily in Brazil , with others in Indonesia and India.

The Forest Guardians – a group of Guajajara people who have battled illegal invasions for years – warned in comments in the Survival International statement that “climate change, fires, deforestation and land encroachment” were affecting the Awá’s way of life.
According to Survival International, many of the guardians have lost their lives trying to protect the territory they share with the Awá.
body_zh: 巴西部落因生活方式受到威胁而陷入孤立原住民
亚马逊土著阿瓦人与村民接触并接受食物带回领土
几个组织周二报道称，大约 20 名原住民在巴西亚马逊雨林中摆脱了与世隔绝，这引发了对该部落领地入侵增加的警报。
据非政府组织生存国际称，自愿隔离的阿瓦人成员于周一抵达一个村庄，并与政府团队进行了一次“历史性的接触”。
他们进入的村庄位于马拉尼昂州东北部的阿拉里博亚原住民领地内，该州是瓜亚加拉族的家乡。
当地社区领导人表示，村民们向这群人提供了食物。
“他们要山药，然后把它们带回森林，”生存国际组织说。
该非政府组织解释说，阿瓦人通常以狩猎和采集为生。然而，他们面临着越来越多的非法伐木者、猎人和牧场主的入侵。
由瓜亚加拉村民拍摄并由生存国际组织发布的这次遭遇的视频显示，一群男人、女人和儿童在森林边缘。
他们部分被植被掩盖，看起来赤身裸体，戴着项链。 The men carry bows and long arrows.
代表马拉尼昂州原住民群体的组织 Coapima 警告说：“一些成员的身体状况，尤其是儿童和老人的身体状况引起了村民的关注，他们注意到明显的严重消瘦迹象。”
科皮马强调了意外接触对这些群体造成的风险，并指出他们特别“容易感染疾病”，而对这些疾病几乎没有免疫力。
负责原住民事务的公共机构 Funai 在发给法新社的一份声明中表示，其技术团队正在密切监视局势并分析有关该群体健康状况的现有信息。
生存国际组织主任卡罗琳·皮尔斯表示，该组织选择摆脱孤立状态是“令人不安的迹象，表明对与世隔绝的人们的森林的持续入侵如何使原本自给自足的原住民陷入真正的危险”。
她说，阿瓦人正被驱赶到“亚马逊雨林中一个越来越小的岛屿，周围充满了破坏”。
据该非政府组织称，已在 10 个国家/地区确定了约 196 个选择隔离生活的“未与外界接触”的民族和群体。
超过 90% 的此类群体生活在亚马逊雨林中，主要分布在巴西，其他分布在印度尼西亚和印度。
森林守护者组织——多年来与非法入侵作斗争的瓜哈加拉人——在生存国际声明中的评论中警告说，“气候变化、火灾、森林砍伐和土地侵占”正在影响阿瓦人的生活方式。
据生存国际组织称，许多守护者在努力保护与阿瓦人共享的领土时丧生。
